key_insight: A deterministic dyadic triadic decomposition makes the Navier-Stokes energy flux fully scale-resolved, showing how local and nonlocal interactions build toward Kolmogorov-like scaling.
engineering_relevance: This gives engineers a clearer structural picture of where energy moves across scales in turbulence models, which can inform analysis, closures, and scale-aware simulation strategies.
method: Decompose the velocity field into dyadic scale bands in Fourier space.
Derive an exact triadic expansion of the nonlinear energy flux across scales.
Separate and bound local versus nonlocal contributions under smoothness assumptions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an analytic, deterministic derivation with absolutely convergent triadic expansion and formal consistency with $-5/3$ scaling, rather than numerical dataset-based validation.
watch_item: The Kolmogorov scaling result is formal and structural, so its practical use depends on the smoothness assumptions and on how well the decomposition captures real turbulent flows.
paper_title: From Triadic Interactions to Kolmogorov Scaling: A Deterministic, Scale-Resolved Formulation of Energy Flux
